texts: I paid the seller directly. Which Superbuy service should I look at?
Read the parcel forwarding guide. It covers items you bought yourself and need received at a Superbuy warehouse. A shopping agent order instead asks Superbuy to make the purchase.
Should I register a forwarding request for an item Superbuy bought for me?
Superbuy says that a purchase made through its shopping agent service does not require a separate forwarding submission. Check the shopping order and its warehouse status first.
Where should I get the address for my forwarding shipment?

Use the receiving address displayed in your own Superbuy forwarding account for the selected warehouse. Copy all the address parts and account-specific identification exactly before sending the seller the delivery instructions.
Can I use the warehouse address from someone else's tutorial?

A screenshot may show an old address or a different user's identifying information. Open your own account, select the applicable warehouse and compare the full address with the seller's order before dispatch.
What if my forwarding item has no marketplace product URL?

Superbuy's forwarding guide describes supplying an item name and type for an already prepared parcel. Describe the actual contents and use the form's current requirements to check whether review is possible.
What do I check before sending a self-purchased item to the warehouse?
Check the forwarding review result, the approved item, the selected warehouse and the receiving instructions. Resolve a restriction or incomplete request before asking your seller to dispatch.
Is the seller's order number the domestic tracking number?

The seller order identifies the purchase. The waybill identifies a physical shipment handled by a carrier. Copy the carrier name and waybill from the dispatch record when completing forwarding logistics.
My seller split a purchase into two boxes. How should I record it?

Keep a separate row for each carrier and waybill. Ask which pieces went into each box, then compare each arrival with the warehouse record. One delivered box does not account for every unit purchased.
Where do I see items that have been stocked at Superbuy?

The official forwarding and app guides direct customers to My Warehouse. Match the entry with your order or forwarding request. Use the domestic carrier's scan to investigate timing when the stock entry is missing.
Which photos help distinguish two otherwise identical garments?
Ask for an overview and a readable size or option label associated with each warehouse entry. Record the item reference beside the photograph before combining anything for delivery.
Can a warehouse photo confirm that an electrical item works?

A picture may show the model and visible condition. Functional testing is a separate question. Ask which inspection is available for that item and whether the requested test can actually be performed.
Should I include an item with unresolved damage in a parcel?

Check its order and contact the relevant service first. Clearly identify the affected unit and ask what remedies remain while it is still at the warehouse. Keep it off the dispatch selection until you have made a decision.
How do I compare a shipping deposit with the final charge?

Record the route, destination, contents, estimated weight and deposit at submission. Compare them with the packed dimensions, verified weight and charge in the parcel record. Check current route terms for the treatment of differences.
Do dimensions from the seller's product page describe my outbound parcel?
They may describe the item or its retail box. International estimates may depend on the outer packed parcel. Record what was measured, including its units and packaging state.
Which packing instructions should I give for fragile parts?

Describe which surfaces need separation, what must stay together, and which protective pieces should be retained. Ask whether the requested packing is available and review any charge before authorizing it.
Why might my selected shipping line change after consolidation?
The packed parcel can differ in dimensions, weight or contents from the original estimate. Check the live list of routes available for the complete parcel and its destination.
Where can I follow a parcel after Superbuy dispatches it?
The app guide directs buyers to My Parcel in the user center. Use the outbound tracking reference on that parcel, keeping earlier seller tracking numbers with their respective domestic shipments.
What should I send support about a delivered parcel missing from My Warehouse?

Include the forwarding reference, warehouse selected, carrier, waybill, delivery scan and expected contents. Explain the specific mismatch and provide the unredacted private details only through the official support channel.
How can I check whether a shipping request applies to one item or the whole parcel?

Read the service name and quantity on the order. For example, a close photo of one item and reinforcement of the outer carton concern different objects. Ask for clarification before paying for an ambiguous request.
Which record should I use for an international delivery issue?

Begin with the outbound parcel reference and current tracking event. If a particular item is affected, add its warehouse entry. Keep the package, label and relevant photos available for the investigation.
Can I use a friend's shipping estimate for my own budget?
Only as a rough comparison. Match the destination, date, route, parcel dimensions, weight and service options. Your own live quote is the relevant estimate for your shipment.
Comparing estimated and packed dimensions in Superbuy's shipping calculator

An estimate based on a seller's product dimensions and a quote based on a closed outbound carton can produce different results even when nothing has gone wrong. The first figure may describe a bare item. The second includes everything that occupies space in transit. Before comparing a Superbuy shipping estimate with a parcel record, identify what each number measures and bring both scenarios onto the same basis.
Collect three measurements, their units and their object

Record length, width and height together. A single “size” such as 40 centimetres cannot tell you whether a box is long and narrow or nearly square. Identify the object measured: loose product, retail box, seller delivery carton or packed outbound parcel. A measurement is useful only when you know which of these four things it describes.

Take a pair of shoes as an example. The foot length on a size chart is a fit measurement. The outsole length describes a shoe. The shoebox dimensions describe a retail package. The external shipping carton may contain the shoebox plus padding and another item. Entering the foot length as the longest side of the parcel because it is the only visible number creates a precise-looking estimate from an unrelated measurement.
Normalize units before comparing anything

Superbuy's shipping calculator displays weight in grams and dimensions in centimetres. Read the labels on the version you are actually using. Convert a weight given in kilograms by multiplying by one thousand. Convert millimetres to centimetres by dividing by ten. Keep the original numbers in your notes as well as the converted values; this makes it easier to identify a transcription error later.

Suppose a seller lists a box as 420 by 260 by 150 millimetres and the scale reads 1.80 kilograms. Its corresponding inputs are 42 by 26 by 15 centimetres and 1,800 grams. If one side is accidentally entered as 150 centimetres, the box in the calculator becomes ten times taller than the box on the desk. A disappearing route or implausibly high figure can be a reason to recheck units before assuming the carrier has changed its prices.
Name the assumptions in the first estimate

Record the destination, warehouse, category and planned contents alongside the estimated weight and dimensions. These fields can affect which results are displayed. Two estimates with identical dimensions but different destinations are not a controlled test of packaging. Likewise, a different item category may change eligibility even if the physical package stays the same.

Write a short scenario summary such as “one pair, original shoebox kept, outer carton dimensions unknown, using seller box dimensions as a lower-information estimate.” This tells you exactly what you will need to replace when the warehouse provides measurements. Avoid describing the provisional result as your confirmed freight. You may have an accurate seller measurement while still missing the relevant shipping measurement.
Calculate the space difference without inventing a freight rule

For a rectangular box, multiply length by width by height to compare volumes. If an illustrative first estimate uses 40 by 25 by 15 centimetres, the rectangular volume is 15,000 cubic centimetres. A measured outer package of 42 by 28 by 18 is 21,168 cubic centimetres. The difference is 6,168 cubic centimetres, around 41 percent more space than the estimate.

That comparison describes geometry only. Whether a particular carrier uses dimensional billing, how it converts volume into a billing weight, how it rounds and how much it charges are separate questions. Read the selected route rules instead of borrowing a divisor from a different carrier's tutorial. A 41 percent increase in volume does not prove that freight increased by 41 percent. The actual weight, route limits and rate bands may matter more.
Measure the longest point that actually travels

Use the maximum outside dimensions of the packed item or carton as instructed by the carrier. Corner protectors, end caps and bulging sides can extend past an otherwise tidy rectangle. Ask which dimensions were returned by the warehouse if the values appear to describe only the item inside. Record measurements in a consistent order and label the longest side explicitly when route limits make it important.

A rolled print is a useful illustration. The artwork size is a flat rectangle. Its tube has a length and diameter. If several tubes are bundled in a rectangular carton, the outbound dimensions are different again. Comparing the flat sheet's height with the bundle's longest side tells you very little. Write down which packing state each entry represents before deciding that one of the measurements must be wrong.
Change one variable at a time

To investigate a quote difference, start from the closest reproducible version of the first estimate. Substitute the packed dimensions while keeping destination, warehouse, item category, weight and route selection constant if possible. Record the new result. Then substitute the packed weight and compare again. If an input makes the original route unavailable, note that as an eligibility change rather than comparing two different services as though they were the same line.

Consider an item weighing 1,800 grams in its seller packaging. Its final packed weight becomes 2,100 grams. If you change the box size, weight and destination at the same time, the resulting difference cannot tell you which factor mattered. A pair of controlled estimates identifies whether one change appears sufficient to alter the quote. The calculator remains an estimate; the exercise is designed to clarify assumptions rather than reproduce a carrier invoice exactly.
Reconcile the deposit separately from optional services

Superbuy's guidance distinguishes the international shipping deposit from final shipping based on verified measurements and the selected service. When looking at a total, separate the freight component from selected packing, other services and any distinct adjustments displayed in the account. Preserve the original currency and keep the actual parcel reference with every amount.

If your card statement is in a different currency, first compare the two Superbuy records in their common transaction currency. Only then investigate any payment conversion. Otherwise a difference in exchange rates can look like a change in packed weight. A useful support question specifies the original estimate, packed measurements, route, deposit and the single unmatched amount. “My shipping changed” leaves too many possible explanations unresolved.
Keep the final comparison useful for the next parcel

Save the accepted packed dimensions, contents, packing treatment and weight after dispatch. This becomes a reference case for a similar future decision, provided you retain its conditions. Two identical retail items may still yield different outer cartons when one is shipped alone and the other is combined with a book or wrapped with additional protection.

Review what your first estimate got right and what changed. Perhaps the scale weight was close but the protective carton was larger. Next time you know which missing measurement deserves attention before you choose a route. The goal is not to predict a shipping price from memory. It is to recognize which assumptions are provisional, replace them with the measured values and understand the resulting choice before committing the parcel to international delivery.

If the account and your worksheet still disagree, include the original units in your inquiry. A support agent can check a photo of the scale and measuring tape more readily than a number stripped of its unit and packing context.

For a two-box comparison, calculate each rectangular volume separately before adding them. Multiplying the sum of the lengths by the sum of the widths and heights produces an imaginary oversized box. Only use the measured dimensions of a single combined carton if the warehouse has actually combined the goods that way. Keep each individual carton measurement beside its corresponding quote.
How to match a domestic tracking number to a Superbuy warehouse entry

A delivery notification from a seller can be accurate while your Superbuy warehouse list still looks incomplete. The two records are answering different questions. One reports what a carrier did with a parcel. The other records what was received, identified and stocked for your account. Before deciding which party to contact, follow the particular box across that boundary.
Draw the short journey first

Start with the journey inside the country where the seller dispatches the goods. Your marketplace order links a buyer and a merchant. The merchant hands a box to a domestic carrier, which transports it to a receiving address. The receiving warehouse then identifies, inspects and records the goods. International shipment is a later choice. A tracking update mentioning delivery on the domestic leg cannot establish that an overseas parcel is on its way.

For an agent purchase, find the Superbuy shopping order associated with the original item. For a purchase you made yourself, find the forwarding request and the logistics information you supplied. Superbuy's forwarding guide directs the user to provide the inbound shipping details after the item is reviewed. Check which of those two starting points describes your case. A shopping order number from a similar purchase can lead you to inspect the wrong record.
Copy the carrier evidence exactly

Open the seller's dispatch detail and identify the carrier and waybill together. Copy the full waybill as text, preserving any leading zeroes. Save the most recent event, its date and its stated location. A screenshot cropped down to the word “delivered” omits the information needed to connect the event to a particular carton. If a platform shows a tracking alias, keep the original carrier number where available.

Suppose two purchases appear in your marketplace history with almost identical titles and consecutive order dates. On one, the waybill ends in 381; on the other, it ends in 318. A glance at the first digits may suggest that both refer to the delivery you just received. Compare the entire string. When you later write to support, paste the complete number rather than the last three digits used in your private notes.
Identify what the last event actually says

Read the wording of the event as well as the status colour. Label created, collected, out for delivery, delivered and returned to sender indicate different stages. A label can exist before the merchant hands over the box. An out-for-delivery update describes work in progress. A delivery event names an endpoint for the carrier's movement; it does not list the contents counted by warehouse staff.

Look at the destination alongside the event. Does the city and receiving address correspond to the warehouse selected on your request? An account login or internal recipient identifier can help connect the parcel with the customer after delivery. If the marketplace receipt shows a different address from the one in Superbuy, keep both records and explain the difference. Do not “correct” the screenshot before sharing it with official support: the original discrepancy may be exactly what identifies the problem.
Look for an intake match in My Warehouse

Open My Warehouse for the relevant account. Superbuy's official guidance identifies this as the place to view stocked items. Review the warehouse entries around the delivery event. Check the item description, purchase or forwarding reference, quantity and available pictures. A translated title may differ substantially from the seller's original wording; use identifiers wherever possible.

An inbound carrier parcel and a warehouse inventory entry need not have the same shape in your notes. One carton might hold several items. One seller purchase might produce two cartons. If the warehouse lists separate goods while your evidence describes a single carrier box, group those entries under the waybill rather than deleting one as a duplicate. Conversely, two received cartons cannot be reconciled solely from one product title without determining what each contained.
Work through a split-delivery example

Imagine buying a desk organiser and a pen tray from one seller. The retailer issues two domestic waybills. The organiser shows a delivery scan, while the tray is still moving. You see one warehouse entry described as a desk accessory. Before reporting a missing piece, compare the first tracking number with the warehouse reference and inspect the photo. If it depicts the organiser, the current records are consistent: one item is stocked and the other is still in transit.

Now change one detail. The merchant says both items were in the first carton and the second number was a cancelled replacement label. The warehouse picture still shows only the organiser. The open question has changed. It now concerns the contents of a delivered carton and the status of a second unused label. Ask the merchant to confirm its packing list. Ask Superbuy which items were recorded under the first waybill. Keep the distinction clear and avoid asking a carrier to locate an item that may never have travelled under its number.
Route the inquiry to the party that can inspect the evidence

If the carrier shows only creation of a label, the merchant can usually clarify whether it actually dispatched that carton. If the event names the wrong destination, ask the sender and carrier about the address they used. If the correct parcel shows delivery to the intended warehouse but you cannot match it with an entry, Superbuy can investigate its receiving records. Explain which of these checks you have already completed.

Use a concise opening sentence: “I am trying to match a domestic delivery to my forwarding record.” Follow with the forwarding or purchase reference, carrier, complete waybill, date and location of the delivery event, and expected product and quantity. State exactly what My Warehouse currently shows. A reply that confirms receipt of the box may still leave a separate question about contents; acknowledge the first point before asking about the second.
Avoid multiplying records while a check is open

It is tempting to enter the parcel again with a slightly different product title, especially if searching your account yields no result. First ask whether the existing forwarding or shopping record can be updated. Duplicate submissions can make it harder to tell which record describes the actual box. A new title cannot change which address is on the label or which carrier made the delivery.

Keep a short activity note with dates and references rather than sending disconnected messages. If support requests a clearer proof of delivery, append it to the same inquiry when possible. If the seller supplies a corrected waybill, label the old one as superseded. This preserves what was known at the time of the first search while directing the next search to the better evidence.
Know when the domestic question is settled

Mark a domestic shipment as matched when you can connect the carrier record, the correct purchase or forwarding request and the relevant warehouse entry or entries. Mark the contents separately if one piece remains unidentified. That division keeps the status accurate: “carton received, tray unconfirmed” tells you much more than simply “delivered.”

Later, if you submit the stocked items for international delivery, save the outbound parcel number in its own place. Look under the parcel record for the international journey. Keep the domestic references attached to the purchases they originally described. If another piece turns up or a seller answers a question much later, you can add that evidence without confusing it with a different shipment heading to your home. If the final warehouse count differs from the seller invoice, keep the count discrepancy open even after matching the waybill. Finding the carton and confirming its contents are separate outcomes.
A self-purchased parcel is missing from Superbuy: prepare an intake investigation

You have a forwarding request, your seller says the package arrived and My Warehouse does not show the expected item. The most useful first step is to build a short investigation with one clearly defined missing link. Establish what the seller dispatched, where the carrier took it and what your Superbuy account shows. Each party can then check the part of the journey it actually handled.
State the problem without deciding the cause

Write a sentence containing an observation and a question. “The domestic carrier records delivery of waybill X to the selected warehouse on Tuesday; I cannot match it to a stocked entry. Can you help identify it?” is specific. It does not require you to decide prematurely whether the merchant, carrier, warehouse or account entry is at fault.

Avoid treating a missing entry as proof that the parcel was lost. The available evidence might instead describe an unused label, a delivery to a different warehouse, an unrecognized sender, an incomplete account identifier or a product recorded under an unexpected name. List only possibilities supported by something in your own records. If the seller has never supplied a collected waybill, the first unresolved step is dispatch, not warehouse intake.
Build a timeline from original records

Create one row per event with the time, source and exact reference. Useful events include the marketplace purchase, forwarding request, review response, seller dispatch notice, carrier collection, last carrier scan and any warehouse message. Preserve the timezone shown by each source when it matters. Two events labelled “Tuesday” can occur on different local dates in the buyer's country and at the warehouse.

Order the events by what occurred rather than the sequence in which notifications appeared on your phone. A delayed email can arrive after a newer carrier update. An order page may show an edited tracking number beneath an older dispatch date. If a time is unknown, leave it unknown. A timeline built from explicit events is more valuable than a polished story that invents the missing transition.
Check the receiving address and account identifier

Open your own Superbuy forwarding instructions and compare them with the address on the seller's confirmed order. Match warehouse, region, street and the account-specific information used to identify incoming shipments. Superbuy's guide explains the purpose of the identification number appearing with a receiving address. A seller may have copied the street correctly while shortening the last field on the printed label.

If you find a difference, capture both records privately and describe it precisely. “The seller receipt shows the correct street but is missing the final identifier” gives the receiving team a concrete search clue. Do not substitute the corrected address for the original evidence. Likewise, do not rely on a profile update to correct a package already in transit. Ask the seller or carrier what address appears on the actual shipment when the order receipt is inconclusive.
Test the tracking number before sending it

Check that the number belongs to the courier that physically handled the parcel. Distinguish it from a seller order, forwarding application, marketplace consolidation number or an international tracking number from a previous shipment. Open the merchant's shipping record and compare the carrier and complete number with what you entered in Superbuy. Leading zeroes, letters and transposed digits can all affect a match.

A merchant may issue a label and then reprint a replacement. Ask which number has an actual collection event. If the replacement is the one that moved, name the original as an unused or superseded reference in the inquiry. That tells support why two numbers appear in the paperwork. If neither number has a collection event, ask the seller for evidence of handover before asking the warehouse to search for a delivered box.
Specify the box and its expected contents

For a single parcel, list the useful physical identifiers: type of item, selected option, quantity, seller name and any packing information provided. For a split delivery, provide a waybill-to-contents map. Avoid assuming that everything on one seller order was packed together. The merchant can often confirm which pieces accompanied a particular label.

Imagine two cartons listed as a bookcase frame and a shelf pack. The frame appears in My Warehouse, but the shelf pack does not. The support inquiry should name the unmatched shelf pack, its own waybill and its expected pieces. Sending only the original order title “bookcase” could lead to a reply identifying the already matched frame. Including the known warehouse entry is useful because it shows exactly which part of the purchase has been accounted for.
Compare intake evidence before choosing the recipient

If the last evidence is a marketplace status saying the seller prepared the order, the seller can clarify actual dispatch. If a carrier records an attempted delivery or an address problem, ask about the unresolved delivery event. If the carrier confirms delivery to the expected destination and the logistics details were recorded, use the Superbuy support route associated with the forwarding request. Each inquiry should ask for an action the recipient can perform.

For a warehouse inquiry, include the request reference, selected warehouse, domestic carrier and waybill, delivery event, expected contents and any existing warehouse record that could be related. Explain which account view you checked. Share full identifying details through the official private channel. Crop unrelated orders and payment information from supporting screenshots, while keeping the specific reference, date and event legible.
Ask one searchable question at a time

A first message might read: “Please check whether the carton under this domestic waybill was matched to my forwarding request. The carrier shows delivery to the selected warehouse. I attach the seller dispatch confirmation and the delivery scan. The expected contents are one shelf pack; the frame from the same seller is already stocked under a separate entry.” Add the real references in the appropriate private fields.

If the response confirms receipt but says the contents were different, the investigation has moved forward. Ask which item was recorded from that waybill and compare it with the seller's packing statement. If the warehouse needs a photo of the physical label, request it from the seller rather than repeatedly resending a screenshot of the product itself. Preserve the question and response together so the next step builds on what has already been established.
Close the case only after the missing link is identified

When an entry appears, compare its physical description and quantity with what was expected. An entry with the same translated product title may belong to an earlier order. Confirm the connection using the forwarding reference, carrier evidence or the warehouse's explicit identification. Record what resolved the discrepancy and retain any outstanding quality or quantity question separately.

A delivery investigation can finish with a matched item, a correction to the sender's record, a carrier inquiry or another documented outcome. Record the actual outcome rather than forcing every case into “delivered.” If you subsequently send the goods overseas, create a new outbound parcel entry. The inbound investigation then remains a complete account of how the warehouse identified the package, ready to consult if the seller or carrier asks about it later.

If you ultimately discover that the parcel was stocked under an unexpected description, note the phrase used by the warehouse and the evidence that established the match. It can be useful to record a picture reference and the original seller description next to that entry. The warehouse title may stay unchanged even after support confirms its identity. If it is later split across parcels, retain the original reference beside both outbound records so you can identify the right portion at delivery.
Using Superbuy on a phone: check the option that reaches your shopping order

A mobile screen makes it easy to save a photograph and hard to see the complete purchase in one view. The image, selected variant, quantity and price can appear on separate panels. Superbuy's app guide describes finding a product, selecting its options and asking the agent to purchase it. Use those stages as checkpoints. The aim is to carry your intended selection all the way from the seller listing to the paid order.
Begin with a recoverable product reference

Before switching apps, save the original marketplace product link. If a share sheet includes promotional text around the address, preserve the underlying listing address where possible. Make a short note of the seller and item identifier. That gives you a way back if opening a shopping link changes the active browser tab or if a marketplace app returns to its home screen.

A screenshot is a useful companion, especially for a distinctive pattern. It rarely contains all the information required to identify a live listing. The same studio picture can appear on multiple products or be reused by different sellers. A saved image showing a blue notebook does not establish which shop offers it, what paper is inside or whether the photograph depicts the cover only. Save the link first and the picture second.
Check the handoff to Superbuy

The official app guide describes searching from the home screen and recognizing certain product links. Use the available entry method on your device. When the agent page opens, compare its product and seller information with what you intended to import. Do not infer a match merely because the first image looks familiar.

If the device opens a search result list rather than the exact product, treat this as a new identification step. Compare the original item number where available, then examine the option set and seller details. A search result with another seller and a lower displayed price is a separate purchasing choice. If you still want it, review it as a new listing rather than silently replacing the earlier selection in your notes.
Read the entire option panel

Open the selector and identify the dimensions of the choice. A product can have colour, size, bundle contents and quantity, each controlled separately. Some combinations may be unavailable even if the colour swatch itself appears selectable. Make the complete selection, then look for the final summary. Scroll horizontally or expand text where the interface abbreviates a long option label.

Imagine a listing for sketchbooks with “black A5, dotted” and “black A5, blank.” The thumbnail can be identical because it shows the closed cover. If your requirement is blank paper, the word at the end is the decisive feature. Save the complete option text. A hand-written note saying “black notebook” loses precisely the detail that the warehouse may later need to verify.
Check the unit and the number you are ordering

A quantity selector counts the unit represented by the chosen option. If the option says a pack of three, setting the quantity to two can mean six physical pieces. If the price refers to a replacement cover, it may omit the book displayed in a lifestyle photograph. Read the unit description and the subtotal after making the selection.

An illustrative check is to write “two packs, three pieces per pack, six pieces expected” before checkout. Compare that reading with the displayed quantity and the merchant's option description. If one screen describes two units and another describes six pieces, they may be consistent. If you cannot explain the difference yourself, ask the agent to clarify before authorizing a purchase. Do not try to fix an unknown unit by choosing a larger number and hoping the seller interprets it correctly.
Use the cart as a final specification

After adding the item, reopen its cart line. Check the exact option, quantity, seller and current price. A previously saved cart item can survive between sessions and look like a second copy of today's item. Compare dates or line details before changing quantities. Replacing an old option with a new line can leave both selected for payment.

Read each charge in context. Superbuy's shopping guide separates the purchase and any applicable domestic delivery from the later international parcel process. Save the currency and total on the purchase screen. If a catalogue converts a price for convenience, use that figure for rough comparison and use the actual checkout amount for your payment record. A mobile notification quoting a card amount may use a different currency and cannot by itself identify the selected item.
Write notes that resolve a decision

An order note works best when it identifies an option the agent can check. Instead of “as pictured,” write the original seller option followed by your explanation of what matters. For a sketchbook, that might be “black cover, A5, blank pages; please ask before replacing with dotted paper.” If the seller allows customization, reproduce spelling and case carefully and specify any uncertainties before payment.

Avoid using a note to contradict a selected option without checking whether the seller can supply the request. Selecting the cheaper cover and writing “complete book please” does not establish that the full set has been purchased. If a required combination is absent from the live selector, ask whether it is available and what it costs. Save the response with the order confirmation.
Follow the shopping order into the warehouse

Once payment is complete, save the Superbuy order reference. Use the order inquiry or other contact route shown for questions about that purchase. A question about an unavailable colour belongs with the shopping record; a shipping quote for an assembled outbound parcel belongs later in the process. Naming the stage helps the person responding understand what action you expect.

When the item is stocked, the official guide points you to My Warehouse. Reopen your note alongside the warehouse pictures. Check what is visible: a closed black cover might match the colour but not the page ruling. If the interior matters, request a view that shows the relevant feature and check the available inspection options for that item. Keep the item reference in the request so a photo of a similar notebook cannot be accidentally used to make your decision.
Recover calmly if an app switch loses your place

If the app closes during checkout or payment, inspect the order and payment records before repeating the action. A checkout screen reopening at its beginning does not establish whether the payment succeeded. Look for the order reference, the amount, currency and latest payment state. If they disagree, use the official support channel with those details. Avoid creating a second order merely to see whether the first one existed.

Finish by keeping a compact mobile record: seller link, complete option, unit and quantity, paid order reference and the feature that must be checked at intake. Once you have those fields, changing devices or reopening a cart becomes manageable. You can explain exactly what you commissioned, recognize your own warehouse item and handle freight as a new decision when the item is ready. That continuity is more valuable than any particular arrangement of buttons in an app update.

For purchases made for someone else, send the final selected option back to that person before checkout if the choice was ambiguous. Ask them to confirm the exact attribute at issue, such as ruling, sleeve length or included accessory. A reply approving a clear written specification is easier to use later than a thumbs-up attached to a general product photo. Save the final confirmation alongside the original order record.
Organizing Superbuy warehouse entries before you select a parcel

A warehouse list starts as a set of arrivals, then gradually becomes a set of decisions. One jacket is ready, another needs a measurement, a gift must keep its box and a replacement has arrived for an older order. Selecting every visible entry can mix those decisions together. Organize the entries around what you can actually dispatch.
Keep the warehouse reference as the anchor

Start a row for each relevant warehouse entry. Copy the reference as displayed, the associated purchase or forwarding record and a description you can recognize later. A translated product name can be ambiguous. A reference combined with a precise description, such as “navy medium, plain cuffs,” helps you distinguish a unit from a similar item bought several days earlier.

Do not make the seller order the sole key in your record. A seller order can produce several warehouse entries. A forwarding parcel can contain goods from more than one purchase. A replacement may resemble the original so closely that both titles appear identical. Keep a separate field for the event linking the entries, such as “replacement for original entry” or “second unit from same order,” instead of renaming both goods as though they were one.
Record a decision, an unresolved question and an owner

Give each entry a practical state. Useful examples include ready to ship, awaiting a measurement, awaiting seller information, return under discussion and deliberately held for another item. These are your private working notes; use the actual platform status separately. The point is to record what you personally need before allowing that item into an outbound parcel.

For every open question, name who can answer it. The retailer may know whether an accessory belongs to a particular bundle. Warehouse staff may be able to show whether that accessory is physically present. You can decide whether a small cosmetic mark is acceptable. If a row merely says “check,” nobody knows whose action will close it. Replace that word with “waiting for a photograph of the inside label” or “compare width with my own jacket.”
Work through a mixed order

Imagine four entries. The first is a navy shirt whose size label and measurements you have accepted. The second is another navy shirt, this time in the larger size ordered for someone else. Its label is unreadable. The third is a mug with a fragile handle. The fourth is a book that you want to keep in its original slipcase. Four stocked entries do not automatically make four dispatch-ready entries.

Mark the first shirt ready. Hold the second for identification. For the mug, record its current condition and the packing protection you require before it travels. Mark the book ready subject to retaining the slipcase. This leaves you with one item to inspect and two item-specific packing instructions. Those outcomes are much more informative than a list in which everything says “arrived.”
Find restrictions before grouping goods

Check the live shipping options appropriate to the contents and destination before assuming everything should travel together. An item with a battery, a fragile shape or unusual dimensions may change the usable route list. Identify those properties from the actual item information. A vague catalogue category such as accessories rarely provides enough detail to settle shipping eligibility.

Use possible groups for planning. One group might contain ordinary clothing ready now; another might contain the fragile item whose packing is under discussion. Record which items and packing assumptions went into each estimate. If a route disappears after you add a particular entry, investigate that change before comparing freight totals. Adding a new item does not guarantee that the original route and service conditions survive unchanged.
Track time at item level

Check the current storage information for each entry in your account. Arrival, intake and the deadline displayed for that specific entry are more useful to you than the date you first found the product online. An older item can be approaching a decision point while a newly stocked item from the same seller has more time available. A single date attached to the planned parcel hides that difference.

If a seller issue is still open, record its own action deadline independently. A storage allowance and a seller return opportunity answer different questions. Waiting for one more order to consolidate freight can be reasonable for a confirmed item and unwise for an item with an unresolved defect. Read the conditions applicable to your purchase before letting a planned shipping date control an unrelated return decision.
Prevent mistakes when identical goods are involved

Use a consistent sequence for similar units. Compare the first order note, the corresponding warehouse reference and its photos together. Finish that match before opening the next nearly identical item. If a photo lacks a useful feature, write down exactly what evidence is missing. Two garments with the same front graphic may need different label views to establish which belongs to each recipient.

A practical example is two dark sweatshirts ordered in medium and large. One warehouse picture may show a marked large label while the other shows only a folded front. Do not label the folded one medium solely by elimination if the other order is still in transit or could have been mispacked. Ask for the identifying view tied to the ambiguous entry. Once confirmed, record which unit has which label and the date of that check.
Translate item notes into parcel instructions

Before submission, transfer only the instructions that apply to the chosen parcel. A note to retain a collector's sleeve belongs with the specific book. Reinforcement of an outer carton concerns the entire parcel. Describe the object and action together so that one instruction does not inadvertently override another, particularly when removing some packaging while keeping other pieces intact.

For the mug and book example, “remove all packaging” conflicts with retaining the book's slipcase and may remove protection from the mug. A more useful instruction identifies the outer delivery materials that can be removed, the retail pieces that must remain and the fragile surface requiring protection. Ask whether the requested treatment is available. Save the accepted instruction alongside the eventual packed parcel record.
Reconcile the submitted selection

When you submit goods for delivery from My Warehouse, compare the selected entries with your ready list one final time. Check reference, option, count and packing instructions. Save the outbound reference when issued and attach it to the selected entries. Leave the unselected items showing their own states; moving three items into a parcel does not resolve a fourth item's outstanding measurement request.

After dispatch, use the outbound parcel record for international tracking. Keep the original warehouse links until delivery is complete. If a parcel arrives with three items when you expected four, your record should immediately tell you whether a fourth item was actually selected or deliberately held. That single distinction can save a lengthy search through seller histories, carrier scans and nearly identical photos.

A good warehouse list is short enough to maintain and specific enough to answer the next decision. If a row contains a reference, physical identity, readiness, open question and eventual parcel, it can follow an item from intake to dispatch without losing the details that made you choose it.

For gifts going to different recipients, add the destination group to each entry before comparing combined parcels. A single low freight quote to your address says nothing about the cost of redistributing the contents afterwards. Grouping by intended recipient first can expose a shipping choice that a simple total of warehouse weights conceals.
Receiving a multi-box purchase at Superbuy without losing track of its pieces

A single purchase can generate two exceptions that look like opposites. One warehouse entry looks incomplete because a second box is still travelling. A second entry looks like a duplicate because the product name matches the first. Both can describe a correctly split purchase. To work out what arrived, count purchases, cartons and individual pieces separately.
Define the unit the seller agreed to supply

Start with the paid option rather than the lead photograph. A listing showing a desk and chair might sell a desk only, a chair only or a package containing both. The unit on the receipt determines what you should expect to account for. Write it in plain language. If the seller calls a set “one unit,” list the pieces you expect inside it without turning those pieces into additional purchased units.

Suppose you ordered two identical table lamps. The merchant confirms that each lamp comprises a base, shade and fittings packet. Your purchase record therefore describes two units and six expected components. It still tells you nothing about how many boxes the merchant will use. The seller might send each complete lamp separately, group the bases together or place both sets in one outer carton. You need a packing statement to connect those counts.
Ask for the box map before comparing photos

Ask the seller how many parcels were actually handed over and which carrier number belongs to each. If the merchant supplied a packing list, copy its wording. When contents by box are unknown, say so in your notes. An honest blank tells you what remains to be established. A guessed assignment may silently convert a normal arrival into a false missing-item report.

Give boxes short names in your own notes while keeping the complete carrier number. For the lamps, “box ending 482, expected both bases” is more useful than “large box.” A repacked carton can look different from the seller's photograph, and dimensions can be reported in different orientations. If the waybills came from different carriers, include each carrier's name. Two similar strings can have different meanings in different tracking systems.
Compare deliveries one by one

Read the status for every waybill independently. If two boxes left together, they can still receive scans at different times. A single order-level status on a marketplace may summarize part of the purchase. Open the underlying delivery details and note the latest event for each actual box. Keep a cancelled label separate from a waybill associated with a collected parcel.

In the lamp example, the box expected to hold the two bases has a delivery scan, while the box containing shades and fittings is still in transit. A warehouse record with two bases is consistent with those facts. Mark the bases as accounted for and the other four components as pending. Do not report two missing lamps simply because the original order quantity was two. The meaningful outstanding question is whether the second carton has been delivered and identified.
Connect warehouse entries to physical contents

Once goods are stocked, Superbuy's guides direct users to My Warehouse. Inspect item names and photographs alongside your box map. Decide what each picture actually shows. A closed retail carton labelled “shade set” can support identification of a carton without establishing the count or condition of its contents. A visible pair of shades does not establish that both fittings packets are present.

If the arrangement is ambiguous, ask for an inventory check that someone can carry out. An example request is: “For the warehouse entry linked to the domestic waybill ending 482, please confirm whether it contains two lamp bases and whether any fittings packets were recorded with them.” Include the full reference in the private inquiry. Keep the question about contents separate from a second question about damaged finish or measurements. Each has a different piece of evidence that can settle it.
Handle an unexpected third carton

A merchant may send a small accessory separately without updating the initial packing summary. If a later tracking notice arrives, do not alter the older record to make it appear that you always expected three boxes. Add a dated update naming the source of the new information. Identify which component moved from a previous expectation into the additional carton.

Suppose the merchant reports that the fittings packets were sent by a different carrier. The original second carton is now expected to contain shades only. If the warehouse confirms two shades, that carton can be marked complete even though the overall purchase is still incomplete. Record the third waybill and its expected two fittings packets. This simple distinction matters if the first two cartons are ready to dispatch and the third is delayed.
Decide whether to wait or ship part of the purchase

An availability decision and a packing decision are separate. You might know exactly where every unit is but still need to decide whether partial international delivery serves your purpose. For a modular lamp, shipping the bases without fittings can leave you with two unusable pieces at home. For several independent notebooks, an early partial shipment may be more practical. Describe the consequence of dispatching the available pieces before comparing prices.

Check the applicable storage position and live parcel options for the actual entries. Compare like assumptions. A partial shipment today and a later shipment of accessories may incur two separate outbound charges. A combined parcel later may have different dimensions, packaging needs and route eligibility. Treat each price as a quote for a named set of contents. Nothing about a domestic seller's choice of box count guarantees which outbound packing arrangement will suit you.
Prepare an exception record the warehouse can investigate

If the carrier shows all boxes delivered but the account reflects only some of the contents, build a compact exception report. State the merchant order, each carrier and waybill, the expected contents of each carton, and the warehouse entries found. Then name the single unmatched box or missing component. Distinguish the seller's statement from the warehouse photo; being clear about the evidence makes it easier to decide whether the next check belongs with the seller or the receiving team.

Avoid sending ten loosely related screenshots. Select the order confirmation establishing quantity, the dispatch statement establishing box allocation, the specific carrier event and a warehouse image showing the discrepancy. If a screenshot covers other orders or personal information, limit what you share to what the official support channel needs. Retain the originals privately in case a clearer view is requested.
Reconcile the set when dispatching or unpacking

When all expected pieces are accounted for, write a closure note naming the contents accepted. For the lamps it might read, “Two bases, two shades and two fittings packets checked against the seller confirmation; warehouse entries A, B and C belong to this purchase.” Keep any visible defect or disputed measurement as its own open issue until resolved. A complete component count alone does not settle condition.

If you later combine these goods into one international parcel, attach the outbound reference to that group of warehouse entries. When the shipment reaches you, unpack against the component list rather than trying to remember the merchant's domestic carton arrangement. The seller might have sent three boxes and the international packer might use one. Your original list of required pieces remains useful through either packing choice, and it gives you a precise starting point if something is absent at delivery.

Check loose hardware against the assembly instructions when those instructions are available. A photograph of several small metal pieces rarely establishes which fasteners belong to which unit. Ask the merchant for the expected count by type and keep that statement with the parts list rather than relying on the total weight of the hardware bag.
Registering a Superbuy forwarding shipment before your seller sends it

The easiest time to connect a self-purchased item with its warehouse record is before the seller prints a label. You can still change an address, ask what the box will contain and correct a description without having to trace a parcel in transit. Use Superbuy's forwarding guide alongside the instructions in your own account. The sequence matters more than the position of any individual button.
Make an accurate description from the seller order

Open the original purchase confirmation. Write down the merchant, product name, chosen option, number of units and item type. Use words that distinguish the actual thing inside the box. “Case” could describe a suitcase, a phone cover or a protective box for a camera. “Fabric camera pouch, small, empty” communicates more to someone reviewing what is being sent. Be equally precise when equipment includes batteries, accessories or detachable components.

For a set, distinguish the unit sold from the number of physical pieces. One table-tennis set might contain two paddles and several balls. One seller order for two such sets is two ordered units with several components inside. Tell the warehouse how the seller describes the quantity and keep a separate components note if a missing piece would matter. A catalogue photograph of two paddles is insufficient on its own to establish what the selected option includes.
Use the form that corresponds to your own shipment

Superbuy describes forwarding submissions for an already prepared parcel and for products associated with an online listing. Follow the option that fits what you actually have. If a relative is sending a used item, do not paste a different retailer's link simply to make the fields look complete. Describe the physical item and consult the account form or support about required information.

A listing link is helpful when it matches the item. Save the option as well as the general address. A seller can edit a listing after your purchase, or one listing can combine a base model with a more elaborate option. The person reviewing a forwarding request may see the current page; your original confirmation records what you bought. Keep the two together and indicate any difference that affects what should arrive.
Check the selected receiving warehouse

Use the warehouse shown for your request and the complete receiving instructions associated with your account. A warehouse photograph on a forum, an address from a previous order and a friend's saved checkout address are poor substitutes. Superbuy's guide explains that a unique identifier at the end of a user's address can help identify a parcel. Treat it as part of the address when preparing the seller's delivery details.

Consider a marketplace form that splits the address into region, city, district, street and extra details. Copying a whole address into the street field can duplicate the district while omitting the final identifier. After saving, read the address the way it will print on the label. Compare each part with the Superbuy address from top to bottom. If the seller must enter the address manually, ask them to confirm the completed destination before handing the box to a carrier.
Obtain the review result before promising dispatch

The official forwarding process puts review before sending the parcel. Wait for the result attached to the actual request and follow the current instructions or deadline shown there. A product of a similar type having passed previously does not establish whether this shipment is acceptable. The item, origin, warehouse and planned service can differ. If the review requests more information, answer the question as asked.

This is important if a merchant offers rapid dispatch. Tell the seller when you expect to provide the approved destination instead of guessing an address to satisfy a checkout countdown. If the seller has already dispatched the goods, do not describe them as still awaiting shipment. Record the time, address used and waybill; ask Superbuy which steps apply to an inbound parcel that has already left. A second submission cannot physically redirect it.
Add the domestic carrier and the right number

When the merchant issues the shipping notice, copy the carrier name and its waybill. Keep the original string of characters, including leading zeroes. A marketplace purchase number can appear near the carrier number and look equally plausible. Test your interpretation by opening the tracking detail associated with that particular shipping notice. The number should correspond to that delivery leg.

If a shop first creates one label and later replaces it, keep both notices but mark which label was actually used. Ask the seller which carrier collected the box. An old label may remain on an invoice even when no parcel moved under it. Update the forwarding logistics information as the account permits; if a field is locked, provide the corrected reference through official support.
Prepare for sellers who split a delivery

A request describing three units does not guarantee one carton. A merchant may send what is available first and dispatch the remainder separately. Ask for a list matching pieces to carrier numbers. If there are two boxes, label them in your notes by their actual waybills. Avoid calling one “the second parcel” without a number, because the second box sent can arrive first.

Imagine a lamp body and shade purchased together. The seller packs the metal base in a small carton and the fragile shade in a larger one. The carrier delivers the base on Monday and the shade on Wednesday. You can reconcile that outcome if your notes identify each box and its expected contents. A single row stating “lamp delivered Monday” makes Wednesday's box look unexpected and Monday's receipt look complete. This example illustrates record keeping; check which information the current forwarding form needs for each waybill.
Confirm intake without assuming the contents

Look at the warehouse record after the domestic carrier reports delivery. The delivery scan identifies a carrier event. A stocked entry identifies goods entered in the warehouse system. Compare the reference, name, quantity and any available photographs. If the incoming parcel contained two items, check both. A photograph of an opened carton can establish that something arrived without settling whether the full order is present.

If the entry differs from your forwarding description, preserve the original request and ask about the specific mismatch. For example, “The second waybill was expected to contain one white shade; the warehouse entry shows a metal base. Can you match the received contents to these two waybills?” is more actionable than “My parcel is wrong.” Include enough context to locate the box without sharing private address details in a public forum.
Close the inbound record before arranging overseas delivery

Once the expected units are accounted for, record their warehouse references beside the seller order. Keep any unresolved discrepancy visible before selecting items for international shipment. If an item needs a photo, an identifying label read or an answer from the merchant, complete that check while the warehouse can still inspect it. Only the confirmed goods should enter your outbound packing plan.

Your final record should let you answer a simple question without reopening five websites: what arrived, under which domestic waybill, for which approved request, and what will happen to it next? Keep the outgoing parcel number in a new field when one exists. The forwarding request, incoming carton and international parcel represent different stages. Preserving the links between them makes later tracking and customer-service questions considerably easier.

If the seller ships a replacement later, treat the new waybill as another incoming shipment in your records and ask what the current forwarding procedure requires. Labelling the new entry as a replacement explains its relationship to the purchase without falsely implying that both units arrived in the first box.
Preparing useful packing instructions before a Superbuy shipping estimate

A pre-packing measurement is useful when it resolves a particular uncertainty. It may tell you whether a long item fits a route limit, how large a box becomes when fragile pieces are protected, or which goods can reasonably travel together. “Find the cheapest shipping” leaves the packer guessing which requirements are negotiable. Tell them what has to survive the journey and what information you need to decide.
Identify the decision that requires a packed parcel

Write one question before choosing a service. For example, “Can the poster tube and two folded shirts travel together within the length allowed by the route I am considering?” or “How large is the carton when the retail presentation box and corner protection are retained?” Both questions specify a physical arrangement and an outcome you can act on.

Open the service options actually offered for your parcel. Names, charges and the actions authorized by a service can vary. Check whether you are requesting measurements, asking for a shipping recommendation or authorizing dispatch. If you want a result before choosing a route, say that plainly and confirm that the selected service provides it. A measurement request and consent to ship answer different questions.
Fix the contents before asking for measurements

Record every warehouse reference and quantity to include. Remove entries still awaiting a size check, exchange or decision. If you need two scenarios, give each a short descriptive name. “Shirts only” and “shirts plus framed print” remain clear even if someone reads the request tomorrow without your spreadsheet open.

Suppose you estimate two shirts, then add a rigid poster tube after receiving the dimensions. The old result is still a valid observation about the two-shirt parcel, but it tells you little about the new parcel's longest side. Conversely, taking a small item out of a parcel can leave the outside dimensions unchanged if another piece determines the box size. Never adjust a prior packed measurement by subtracting an item's catalogue length.
Say which packaging to keep and which to remove

Use three groups: materials that must stay, materials that may be removed and materials whose treatment requires your approval. Apply the labels to recognizable pieces. “Keep the illustrated retail sleeve on the book; discard the plain domestic shipping carton if safe; ask before removing the hard inner case” is more precise than “remove unnecessary packaging.”

Explain why an unusual piece matters. A kraft sleeve may look disposable to someone packing hundreds of ordinary goods but belong to the presentation of a gift. A cheap foam insert can hold a fragile component away from a hard edge. The purpose lets the packer propose a suitable substitute where your written instruction cannot be followed exactly. Ask for the available option and price before committing to material changes.
State what must not touch or bend

Describe the vulnerable surface rather than simply calling an object fragile. For a book, corners and the spine might be the critical points. For a mug, the handle joint deserves attention. A rolled print could be harmed by a crushed tube or by loading a hard item against the end cap. Ask how the service can separate, immobilize or support the relevant component.

Imagine packing a mug, a sweatshirt and a hardback book. It might seem that the sweatshirt can protect everything. If the book can slide against the handle, however, adding soft fabric somewhere else in the box does not resolve that contact. State the desired result: keep the hard book away from the handle, protect the book corners and retain sufficient cushioning around the mug. Leave the exact packing method to the available service unless you need a particular material.
Specify the measurements to return

Ask for the actual packed weight and the three outer dimensions of the closed parcel, with units. If the shape is irregular, ask which outermost points were used. A tube's length or a protruding protector can determine a critical dimension. Photographs showing the measuring tape can help resolve a question about orientation, but they do not replace a clearly stated set of figures.

Keep packing measurements separate from the product specifications. A seller might describe a poster as 30 by 40 centimetres, while the packed tube is longer than either edge because it includes end protection. A box may have one height printed on its side and a different actual height after its flaps have been adjusted. For a route comparison, ask for the dimensions that describe the final sealed configuration.
Compare the outcome with the right route inputs

Superbuy's shipping calculator requests the destination, warehouse, weight, size and item category. Use the same inputs as the measured parcel when comparing the resulting options. Weights shown in kilograms may require conversion if the form asks for grams. One kilogram equals one thousand grams. Copying 2.4 into a grams field misstates the input by a factor of a thousand.

For an illustrative calculation, a packed parcel measuring 40 by 30 by 20 centimetres occupies 24,000 cubic centimetres. A second packing option measuring 40 by 30 by 15 occupies 18,000. That is a reduction of 6,000 cubic centimetres, or one quarter of the first volume. It does not follow that the shipping charge falls by one quarter. Check each eligible route's actual billing and size rules and whether the protective treatment still meets your needs.
Keep conflicting instructions out of the request

Read your instructions once from the packer's point of view. “Keep all retail packaging” conflicts with “remove shoeboxes” unless you identify which box the exception covers. “Keep flat” conflicts with rolling the same print. “Repack into the smallest possible box” may conflict with the space required around a fragile joint. Resolve these before paying for preparation.

A useful order of priorities is physical constraints first, preferences second and a request for advice if both cannot be met. For instance: “The book must stay flat with its sleeve. If a smaller carton would require bending the cover, keep the larger carton and return its measurements.” This gives the packer permission to preserve the important requirement while still helping you compare the result.
Record what the result authorizes

When the measurement comes back, attach it to the exact item list and packing description. Write down the date, measured values and any optional charge. If you ask for a different arrangement later, label it as a new scenario. Keeping both makes it possible to explain why a route shown for the first version may disappear for the second.

Before submitting for overseas delivery, compare the final selection with the measured one. Did another item arrive? Did you ask staff to keep a box that the first estimate removed? Did the destination change? Each is a reason to revisit the quote. The benefit of a rehearsal is knowing what was measured and being able to use that observation. A precise request gives you a decision you can make confidently even when the cheapest eligible route is different from the one you originally expected.

For future orders, preserve only useful comparisons. A record saying “foam corners increased the longest side by four centimetres on this framed piece” can guide a question next time. A record saying “this route is always cheaper” loses the conditions that made the earlier result relevant.

When the most important outcome is a strict limit, make that visible in the request. Record the route and the limit you read, then ask for the actual outer measurement. A response saying that the parcel is compact may be accurate as a description but still leave you unable to decide whether that route is available.
Superbuy shopping agent or parcel forwarding: which order should you create?

A shop link in a spreadsheet tells you where an item is listed. It does not tell you who will buy it. On Superbuy, the answer to that question determines whether you need a shopping order or a forwarding request. Choose before money changes hands: the same pair of shoes can travel through the same warehouse under either arrangement, but the person responsible for the purchase and the record that identifies the shipment are different.
Follow the payment to the seller

Start by asking who is going to pay the marketplace seller. If you have picked a listing and want Superbuy to buy it for you, use the shopping agent process. Superbuy's app guide describes choosing the product options and quantity, paying for the purchase and any applicable domestic delivery, and then letting the agent contact the seller. Your first useful reference is the shopping order.

If you have already bought the shoes from the seller, you have a purchase record somewhere else. Paying for another shopping order in Superbuy could commission a second pair. The forwarding process is designed to register goods that someone else will send to the warehouse. Locate the seller's confirmation, check the receiving instructions and register the parcel under the applicable forwarding procedure. If the seller has already dispatched it, tell support the true status when asking what can still be matched.
A seller link is useful in both workflows

A product link can identify the intended purchase in a shopping order. It can also help describe the contents of a forwarding request. Its presence on a form does not turn forwarding into a purchase. Look at what the service will do next. Will someone contact the merchant and buy the item? Or are you supplying information for a parcel that you or your seller will send?

Consider an illustrative case. You find a small stationery set on a marketplace and save its link. Nobody has paid. You want the agent to select the navy cover and purchase one set. Your instructions should identify the cover, quantity, exact seller option and anything you need clarified. Contrast a second case: the seller has already accepted your payment for a navy set and asks for a local delivery address. You now need the correct warehouse destination and a way to identify the resulting package. A new instruction to purchase stationery does not solve that problem.
Know who can answer the next question

For an agent purchase, communicate order questions through the agent order. If the retailer changes the available colour after you pay, ask about that order before accepting a substitution. Keep the original option text and confirm whether the proposed replacement still meets your needs. The relevant question at this stage concerns the purchase from the merchant.

With forwarding, the seller relationship may be your own. If the merchant has not dispatched the goods, ask that merchant for dispatch information. If a carrier has delivered a package to the Superbuy address but you cannot find its warehouse entry, gather the waybill and forwarding reference for the warehouse. Sending a refund question to a warehouse that did not buy the item can waste time while the seller's return conditions continue to apply.
Make a budget for the route you actually use

Write down what has already been paid before comparing prices. For an agent purchase, separate the item subtotal and domestic delivery from the eventual overseas parcel. For a self-purchase, the marketplace receipt already represents the goods. Keep that receipt as an item cost even if the forwarding form asks you to record the item's value. Recording its value does not mean you should count a second purchase in your budget.

Imagine a seller invoice of 150 in the seller's currency, plus 10 for domestic delivery. If you paid those amounts directly, your running purchase cost is 160. Entering 150 as an item value on a forwarding worksheet does not raise the running cost to 310. Add actual new charges when they occur, identifying the service and currency for each. These figures illustrate bookkeeping only; the applicable amounts come from your own order.
The receiving address belongs to a specific request

Superbuy's forwarding guide explains that an account-specific identifier helps distinguish incoming parcels. Read the full warehouse address shown in your own account. Compare it to the selected warehouse and to the address the seller has accepted. Pay attention to the final part of the receiving details when copying them into a marketplace form with separate fields.

If a seller truncates a field, compare the saved order address after checkout. Ask the seller whether the complete receiving information will appear on the physical label. If something is missing, keep the carrier reference and tell Superbuy which address the seller actually used. An edited address in your profile does not retroactively alter a label already attached to a parcel.
Keep one record per purchase and one per shipment

A useful shopping note contains a product reference, option, quantity, amount paid and merchant. A forwarding note needs the receiving warehouse, forwarding request, carrier and actual waybill. One purchase can produce several waybills. Several purchases can travel together in one box. Add a link between records instead of treating the shopping number, inbound waybill and outbound tracking number as interchangeable.

For example, a seller may send a notebook today and its separately ordered refill tomorrow. The seller order can be the same on both dispatch notices while the carrier numbers differ. To check whether both pieces arrived, match each waybill and then compare the contents of the warehouse entries. An account search for the ordinary-language title “notebook” alone may miss a refill entered under a different name.
Where the two workflows meet

After intake, the warehouse stage has more in common. The official Superbuy guides direct customers to My Warehouse to review stocked items before choosing what to ship. At that point your decision concerns the physical units in the warehouse. Confirm the relevant options and quantities, resolve any problem you need to address locally, and select the correct units for the international parcel.

Keep the original relationship visible even after consolidation. If two shirts came through agent purchases and a bag came from a shop you paid directly, one outbound parcel may eventually contain all three. A problem with international delivery can concern the entire parcel. A wrong colour on the bag may still lead you back to your direct seller order. A simple list stating who bought each item prevents the combined parcel from erasing that distinction.
Decide what to do when the status is unclear

If you cannot remember whether an order was completed, check the seller account, your payment record and Superbuy's order list before submitting a new request. A saved product or cart entry is not evidence that the seller was paid. A posted payment may also need investigation if its order reference cannot be identified. Record what each system actually shows and ask a specific question about the unmatched record.

Before proceeding, complete this sentence in your own notes: “The seller will be paid by ___, the parcel will be sent by ___, and I will identify it to Superbuy with ___.” If the first blank is the agent, start from your shopping order. If you already paid the merchant, consult the forwarding guide and its review procedure. If any blank is still uncertain, resolve that one point first. It is much easier to clarify a missing reference before dispatch than to distinguish two identical purchases after both arrive. Keep the answer with the original receipt or order confirmation.
Tracking Superbuy photo and packing requests from instruction to result

A note asking for a measurement, a purchased service and a photograph in your account are three different records. They may refer to the same need, but the note alone does not prove that a service was accepted or that the item was inspected as requested. Connect each optional service with the object it concerns and the result you expect to receive.
Decide whether the unit is an item or a parcel

Begin with the thing someone needs to handle. If you want a precise view of a shirt's collar, that is an item request. If you want two goods separated inside a carton, that is a packing request involving a parcel. Reinforcing an outer box and asking for a close-up of a retail label may involve different services, charges and stages.

Superbuy's shopping and forwarding guides describe optional treatments such as removing packaging or reinforcing a parcel. The service offered for a particular item and its applicable terms should be checked in your account. A suggestion on an independent site is a reason to ask about an option, not evidence that any particular service has been selected, paid for or performed.
Turn a general concern into an observable request

A useful instruction states the object, the action and the evidence needed. “Please check the shoes carefully” tells a person little about the decision you are trying to make. “Please show the size labels on both shoes from warehouse entry A in one readable photograph” describes a specific view. If the concern is colour under neutral lighting, ask for that instead of a generic collection of close-ups.

For a measurement, define both endpoints and the unit. A request for the “length” of a coat might mean centre-back length, shoulder-to-hem length or sleeve length. Name which one you intend. Use the same method on a coat you own if fit is the decision. A number written in a message can be useful, but a photographed tape with both ends visible may answer additional questions about positioning.
Separate conditions from instructions
